items.summary: Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leader and Senior Advocate Gaurav Bhatia has filed a defamation case before the Delhi High Court against Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and its leaders Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka. Bhatia has sought ₹2 crore in damages and an injunction against the CJP leaders. He sued the CJP and its leaders after an AI-generated graphic falsely attributed remarks about Swatantra Bhardwaj to Bhatia. Bhardwaj is accused of assault on the father of CJP activist Nishu Azad. The post stated that Bhatia called Bhardwaj a "dimagi naxal". Das shared the graphic on X, prompting Bhatia to deny making the remarks and give him 24 hours to delete the post and issue an unconditional apology. Das, who later deleted the post, clarified on his X account that it was AI-generated, but asked Bhatia whether he “disagreed” with the AI-generated statement. CJP co-convener Ashutosh Ranka allegedly amplified the disputed post by reposting the graphic from Das's account, adding a caption mocking BJP leaders. Ranka had earlier joined Das and other CJP members in demanding action against Bharadwaj over an alleged assault on the father of CJP activist Nishu Azad.

items.title: BAPS and its celibate monks: The organisation at the centre of the Eiffel Tower row
items.summary: A Hindu religious organisation has come under fire in Paris, France after female employees at the Eiffel Tower were allegedly asked to move away or make themselves “invisible” during a private visit by its delegation. This prompted staff to strike and force the iconic landmark to close on September 7. The delegation, comprising around 100 people, was from the Bochasanwasi Akshar Purushottam Swaminarayan Sanstha, or BAPS, a Hindu religious organisation with roots in Gujarat and a large global following. French authorities are investigating the incident after employees said they were instructed to make themselves “invisible” while the delegation passed through the landmark. BAPS is a denomination within the Swaminarayan tradition of Hinduism. A Hindu group with several branches in the UK and US it gets millions in donations and grants every year. Recently, the massive BAPS Swaminarayan temple in Paris was inaugurated. Prime Minister Narendra Modi addressed the inauguration through a video message and described the temple as a milestone in India-France cultural relations. Others believe that Bhagwat has given the RSS a liberal spin in the US, in words he would not use in India. Both these assessments are off the mark. Bhagwat has given near-identical speeches several times in India, including earlier this year. Indeed he told his US audience as much, recalling his 2018 speech given at Nagpur. He uses the same formulations in both the US and India, but in the latter, he is more expansive.
